# Welcome {.unnumbered}

::: {.audience}
For everyone
:::

Jholok helps a jewellery shop know what it has. It keeps a list of your
products, records every piece that comes in or goes out, and helps you count
what is really on the shelves, so you can see what is missing before it costs
you.

This guide is for anyone using Jholok for the first time: the shop's [owner](chapters/glossary.qmd#owner),
the people who approve counts, and the staff who count. You don't need to know
anything about accounting. Each idea is explained the first time it appears,
and every word is in the [Glossary](chapters/glossary.qmd).

## What Jholok is, and isn't

- **It is** a stock list, a record of every piece in and out, and a way to
  count what's on your shelves and see what's missing.
- **It runs on one phone.** Your stock stays on it, not in the cloud. Back it
  up yourself (@sec-keeping-data-safe).
- **It isn't billing software.** It doesn't make invoices or GST returns. It
  can read the stock file your billing software exports, to check a count
  against it (@sec-book-stock).

## How this guide is arranged

- **Start here** takes you to a first count in half an hour
  (@sec-first-count), then walks through a count in full (@sec-a-count).
- **How counting works** explains stock, the ledger and counting in plain
  words, and how a count is checked and finished.
- **Everyday use** sets the shop up, keeps the catalogue and stock up to date,
  and keeps your data safe.
- **Boxes, tags and billing files** is for shops that count boxes of pieces,
  use piece tags or export stock from billing software.
- **Advanced** covers stock that's away from the shop and entries keyed in
  late.
- **From the shop** tells stories from a shop's year.

Each chapter says who it is for, starts with what you'll learn and ends with
what to remember. Chapters you can skip say so at the top, and the "How it
works" parts are folded away until you open them. Words that may be new are
linked to the [Glossary](chapters/glossary.qmd), which starts with the twelve
you need for a count.

### Where to start

- **If you own the shop and are new to Jholok**, start with @sec-first-count.
  The getting-started card on the app's Overview follows the same steps
  (@sec-overview).
- **If you count stock**, keep the two-page quick guide to hand
  (@sec-counters-quick-guide), and read @sec-a-count when you have time, then
  @sec-counting for why counts are blind.
- **If you approve counts**, read those, then @sec-review and @sec-results.
- **If you count alone**, you can skip setting up people: you count, review
  and complete each count yourself (@sec-solo-path).

In the app, **Settings → User guide**, under More, opens this guide. Review's
**?** button opens the chapter on reviewing a count.

## The shop in this guide

Every example and picture uses the same made-up shop, **Jholok Jewellers**,
with its owner Bidisha and staff Sita, Ramesh and Meena. It is the same shop
that the app's demo shows, so what you read here matches what you see on the
screen. None of its stock is real.

## The pictures

The screenshots are of the app on an iPhone, showing the demo shop. Your own
screens show your shop, so the names and numbers will differ, but the screens
are the same.

The pictures of boxes of jewellery are drawn examples that the app uses for
practice, not photos of a real shop's boxes. Counting boxes from a photo is
new, and how well it works on real boxes hasn't been measured yet; the
chapters on box counting say what that means for you.

## Which app this guide describes

This is guide 0.3, for Jholok 0.1. The [What changed](chapters/what-changed.qmd)
page lists what is new in each edition of the guide.
